headline: From Captive Dancer to Sanctuary Life: Odum the Bear Thrives 17 Years After Rescue
meta_description: A sloth bear freed from forced dancing now enjoys a peaceful life at an Indian sanctuary, testament to the long-term care animal rescue requires.
summary_short: Odum, a sloth bear rescued from abuse and named by Julia Roberts in 2009, is flourishing at an Indian sanctuary at age 26, enjoying muskmelon and hammocks.
body:
Seventeen years after being freed from a life of forced performances, Odum the sloth bear is living in quiet contentment at the Bannerghatta Bear Rescue Centre in India. Once exploited by people who made him dance for tourists before locking him in a cage, the bear now spends his days at age 26 eating ripe muskmelon, swimming in his pool, or napping in a specially made hammock. His transformation illustrates both the depth of suffering these animals endure and what dedicated rescue work can achieve.

Odum gained international attention in 2009 when actress Julia Roberts visited his sanctuary while filming Eat, Pray, Love in India. Roberts named the bear Odum, believed to be an old family name, connecting her to his story in a way that helped raise awareness about the cruel trade in dancing bears. Ahead of World Sloth Bear Day on October 12, International Animal Rescue released new photographs of the bear to mark his remarkable recovery and highlight the reality of long-term animal care.

What makes Odum's story particularly significant is not just his rescue, but the ongoing commitment it demands. Alan Knight, president of International Animal Rescue, emphasizes that responsibility does not end when an animal reaches safety. "As he gets older, he will still require the same amount of patience, kindness and specialized care as was necessary to help him recover all those years ago," Knight noted. Odum's journey—from captivity and abuse to a life of safety and dignity—reminds us that true rescue is a lifetime commitment, and that healing, though slow, is possible.
quick_facts: Julia Roberts named the bear Odum during Eat, Pray, Love filming in 2009
Odum now lives at Bannerghatta Bear Rescue Centre in India
The bear is 26 years old and rescued from forced dancing trade
International Animal Rescue released photos ahead of World Sloth Bear Day
